name: Connecting Europe Facility
evidence_rating: thin: budget commitments and project counts only; interim evaluation pending; no causal study of CEF found
summary: The Connecting Europe Facility co-funds cross-border transport, energy and digital networks. By 2025 the transport money was fully committed and calls had been nearly three times oversubscribed, but only a handful of the 600+ funded transport projects were finished. There is no measured evidence yet of effects on trade, energy markets or growth, and the formal interim evaluation was still under way.

indicators.objective: The proposal's financial statement contains no usable LFS indicators (1.4.4 in the extraction covers synergies); key indicators are in Part 1 of the Regulation's annex, with a Monitoring and Evaluation Framework published as SWD(2024) 276; interim evaluation was still under way in Sept 2025

indicators.indicator: Cross-border and missing links, military mobility, alternative fuels infrastructure
indicators.evidence: Calls oversubscribed up to almost 3x; whole transport budget committed by 2025; 600+ projects ongoing but only 23 small projects finished; remaining need EUR 845bn to complete the network.

indicators.objective: Energy: integrate internal energy market (PCIs, cross-border renewables)
indicators.evidence: EUR 3.5bn awarded 2021-2024 (e.g. 16 electricity projects >EUR 2bn incl. EuroAsia interconnector, Baltic synchronisation); some projects delayed by energy and materials price shocks; EUR 430m temporarily moved to transport.

indicators.indicator: 5G along transport corridors; Global Gateway backbones/submarine cables
indicators.evidence: Start delayed; 117 projects worth over EUR 640m funded (51 backbone/submarine cable projects EUR 420m; 25 5G corridor projects EUR 93m); first results only from 2025; portfolio judged on track.

indicators.indicator: Economic and environmental effects of completed networks
indicators.evidence: Not measured; projects mostly not completed. No causal study of CEF grants found.

literature.citation: European Commission (2018), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for the Connecting Europe Facility 2021-2027 (executive summary SWD(2018) 313), SWD(2018) 312
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for the Connecting Europe Facility 2021-2027 (executive summary SWD(2018) 313)
literature.method: ex-ante (MFF programme IA; draws on mid-term evaluation of CEF 2014-2020)
literature.headline: Focused on structure, priorities and delivery of a continued programme; Regulatory Scrutiny Board asked for stronger monitoring and evaluation arrangements; no quantified impact forecast
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's assessment argued for continuing the Connecting Europe Facility with a broader digital and energy scope, but did not forecast measurable economic effects.

literature.citation: European Commission (2025), Progress report on the implementation of the 2021-2027 Connecting Europe Facility for the years 2021-2024, COM(2025) 516
literature.title: Progress report on the implementation of the 2021-2027 Connecting Europe Facility for the years 2021-2024
literature.headline: Transport calls oversubscribed up to ~3x and budget fully committed by 2025, but most projects in early stages (23 of 600+ finished); energy EUR 3.5bn awarded with some delays; digital 117 projects >EUR 640m, start delayed, judged on track; interim evaluation ongoing
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's first progress report shows the money is being committed quickly - transport calls were nearly three times oversubscribed - but few projects are finished, so no results on traffic, energy flows or growth are available yet.

literature.title: Special report 02/2026: EU transport infrastructure - Further delays and some cost increases, but a reinforced governance framework is in place for the future (an update of ECA special report 10/2020)
literature.venue: European Court of Auditors, Special Report 02/2026
literature.method: audit follow-up of eight EU co-funded transport flagship infrastructures: inflation-adjusted cost re-estimation (2019 prices) and schedule tracking to November 2025, plus follow-up of 2020 recommendations
literature.outcomes: cost overruns, delays, EU co-funding (largely CEF grants) for TEN-T megaprojects
literature.headline: Real costs of the eight megaprojects rose a further 24% since 2020 (82% above original estimates), driven by Rail Baltica (+160%) and Lyon-Turin (+23%); they received €7.9 billion in additional EU grants since 2020, and the 2030 TEN-T core network deadline will not be met.
literature.summary_plain: The EU auditors checked eight big EU-funded transport projects again and found they are even later and more expensive than five years ago. Together they now cost almost twice the first estimates, and Europe's core transport network will not be finished by 2030.
literature.period_geography: 2020-November 2025; eight cross-border/national TEN-T projects (incl. Rail Baltica, Lyon-Turin, Brenner, Fehmarn Belt)
literature.quality: Independent audit with transparent cost data; covers CEF-Transport co-funded projects rather than the CEF Regulation's own effect, and the projects predate CEF 2021-2027; descriptive, no counterfactual.
literature.citation: European Court of Auditors (2026), Special report 02/2026: EU transport infrastructure - Further delays and some cost increases, but a reinforced governance framework is in place for the future (an update of ECA special report 10/2020), European Court of Auditors, Special Report 02/2026
